title: Every Cyclotron-fed site learns from its editors' votes
description:
Ryan, 2026-10-29: editor feedback being incorporated into the Cyclotron that feeds the site should be a standard feature of every Papyrus site that uses Cyclotron.

Today the loop is open. Papyrus sends every human accept/reject on a Cyclotron-decided Reference to the site's Cyclotron publication as a feedback operation (router feedback_one), and Cyclotron stores it as a human label. But the hosted standing run is prediction-only: its optimizer is disabled and priming refuses items the run has decided, so votes never change decisions. On 2026-10-29, Ryan's 13 Anth.us votes were recorded and had no effect.

Done when, for every site with a Cyclotron publication and with configuration only:
- votes are turned into a new reviewed context version by a retraining round: examples come from voted items, never an item for its own decision, and agreement is checked on held-out votes;
- a candidate becomes live only if it beats the current version on held-out votes;
- editors can see in the newsroom what their votes did: votes recorded, last round, agreement before and after, and what is live.

Retraining itself is Cyclotron's work (Cyclotron docs/lab-observatory.md, Retraining, steps 2-3). Papyrus owns sending votes, which already happens, and showing the result.
